title: Quantization technical review - Lynx AI
summary: Deep technical review of quantization options (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) and runtime tradeoffs for Lynx AI's chat+retrieval service. Covered expected accuracy regressions, perf/latency numbers, KV cache interaction, batching strategies, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed next steps: Redwood to run benchmark with Lynx test set (2k tokens) on G5-equivalent nodes with INT8 and AWQ profiles, share AWQ tuning notes and patch, and provide dedicated capacity pricing for pilot.
topics: INT8 vs FP8 vs FP16 accuracy tradeoffs
accuracy regressions and mitigation (calibration, mixed precision)
KV cache and cache persistence tradeoffs
VPC / on-prem deployment constraints and KMS integration
next_steps: Redwood: run 2k-token throughput + latency benchmark using Lynx test suite on G5-equivalent with INT8 and AWQ by 2027-09-15
Lynx: provide sample test prompts, evaluation metrics, and a smaller holdout set by 2027-09-10
Redwood: share AWQ tuning notes and a small patch for tokenizer alignment (link) by 2027-09-12
Schedule follow-up call after bench results (30 min) week of 2027-09-20
action_items: Miguel Torres (Redwood SE): run benchmark with INT8, FP8 (if available), GPTQ and AWQ profiles; capture p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, mem footprint by 2027-09-15
Priya Rao (Redwood Research): produce accuracy regression report (perplexity + task accuracy) for AWQ and GPTQ on Lynx holdout by 2027-09-16
Alex Chen (Lynx): share VPC firewall rules and KMS provider details by 2027-09-10
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-08 15:00 PDT | Duration: 65m | Attendees: Sara (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood RE), Alex (Lynx Head Infra), Maya (Lynx ML), Jordan (CTO), Evan (SRE)

00:00 Sara: okay hey everyone thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the quantization technical review focused on the chat + retrieval workload you mentioned, and surface tradeoffs between INT8, FP8, GPTQ and AWQ. Is that agenda still good?
00:12 Alex: yes sounds good, thanks. Quick context: our production serving is a hybrid approach, some hosted endpoints and some on-prem for regulatory customers. Main pain points are p95 latency under 500ms for chat and throughput for long context generation.
00:25 Miguel: great. Can you confirm baseline model and token lengths?
00:28 Maya: we're primarily running a 30B-ish open model fork (we call it lynx-30b), average requests 350 tokens but we have spikes to 2k tokens for long summaries.
00:38 Miguel: perfect. So first slide — INT8 gives large memory and perf gains but can introduce accuracy drops depending on activation distributions. AWQ (a newer weight-quant approach) keeps better alignment in many cases but has different perf profile.
00:50 Jordan: can you explain AWQ vs GPTQ again? I always mix them up.
00:54 Priya: sure — GPTQ is an offline per-layer quantization technique that often adapts well but requires a calibration pass and can be more aggressive, sometimes causing outliers in safety-sensitive prompts. AWQ is aimed at preserving attention matrices better, it tends to maintain quality on generative tasks but runtime support varies across kernels.
01:12 Alex: and FP8? is that an option on G5/G6?
01:15 Miguel: FP8 (E4M3/E5M2 variants) is starting to be available in newer toolchains and hardware. It preserves dynamic range vs INT8 but needs hardware/kernel support; it sits between FP16 and INT8 in accuracy/perf tradeoffs. On our runtime we can compile FP8 paths but perf depends on kernel support — sometimes similar to FP16.
01:34 Evan: any examples of accuracy regressions to watch for?
01:38 Priya: yes. For retrieval-augmented prompts, quantizing the query/key projection can slightly degrade reranking accuracy; for chat generation, you might see increased hallucination rates on narrow factual prompts with aggressive GPTQ. We recommend a mixed approach: quantize most weights to INT8/GPTQ but keep certain layers in FP16 or use per-channel quantization to reduce regressions.
01:58 Miguel: also worth noting KV cache behavior — if you use prefix/KV caching, quantized KV caches can be stored in lower precision to save memory, but we saw small latency jitter on cache reloads when converting back and forth. For very latency-sensitive p95 you may want to keep KV cache in FP16 and only quantize weights.
02:18 Maya: interesting — does Redwood do automatic conversion of KV cache precision based on sequence length?
02:22 Miguel: currently we support policies; we can configure per-route cache precision and have heuristics tied to seq-length distributions. It isn't fully automatic per-request yet, but it's on the roadmap.
02:33 Jordan: about batching — our live traffic is bursty. We worry batching increases p95 beyond our SLO. Thoughts?
02:40 Miguel: batching improves throughput and reduces cost per token, but increases tail latency. We recommend dynamic batching with strict max-latency cutoffs and a small constant-time micro-batch for chat flows. For example, set max queue delay to 8-12ms for p95 targets under 500ms and enable adaptive batch sizes.
02:58 Alex: any numbers you can share now? ballpark.
03:02 Miguel: on G5-like instances with INT8 and 30B model, we see ~1.8x-2.5x tokens/sec vs FP16 depending on sequence length and kernel. AWQ typically sits around 1.5x-2x but with better quality in some tasks. p50 latencies for 350 tokens can be under 120ms with proper batching; p95 depends a lot on queueing and cache hits.
03:25 Priya: also profiling memory — INT8 reduces model memory by roughly 2x vs FP16; GPTQ/AWQ compressed formats vary but give similar memory benefits. That allows larger batch windows but watch for GPU memory fragmentation.
03:40 Maya: for on-prem/VPC, our security team requires KMS integration and no model artifacts leaving the tenant network — is that covered?
03:48 Sara: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and a private control plane. For on-prem we can deploy the runtime inside the customer's VPC or on-prem cluster. We'll need to align on network egress rules and optionally air-gapped setup.
04:02 Evan: curious about kernel maturity — are AWQ and GPTQ kernels production ready? any caveats?
04:08 Miguel: GPTQ kernels are mature in our stack; AWQ kernels are newer and available in our experimental runtime builds. For production pilot we suggest starting with GPTQ/INT8 and running AWQ in parallel labs to validate accuracy before full rollout.
04:22 Jordan: if we do a pilot, can you run our test set and give granular per-prompt deltas so we can triage where regressions happen?
04:28 Priya: absolutely, that's what we recommend. We'll run the full Lynx holdout and output token-level perplexity + task metrics and a ranked list of prompts with largest deltas.
04:36 Alex: one more ops question: cold start memory and warmup costs for quantized models?
04:41 Miguel: quantized models often have faster cold start in terms of memory footprint, but warmup (loading kernels, JITing) can add a little real time. If you keep warm instances by dedicated capacity you avoid that; cold autoscale does incur a few seconds overhead.
04:56 Maya: any simple mitigations for hallucinations after quantization?
04:59 Priya: calibration datasets and selective FP16 retention are effective. Also temperature and sampling tweaks help; we've seen that small prompt engineering changes reduce hallucination spikes post-quant.
05:12 Sara: okay I want to call out recommended pilot config: run two branches — (A) GPTQ/INT8 with per-channel quant on critical layers and FP16 for output/layernorm; (B) AWQ profile with same selective FP16 retention. Measure p50/p95, tokens/sec, and downstream task accuracy.
05:30 Alex: that sounds good. Who's responsible for running the bench?
05:33 Miguel: Redwood will run initial bench on our infra and then reproduce on your VPC if you provide access and the small holdout. We'll produce detailed artifacts and a spreadsheet — we'll share links.
05:45 Jordan: about cost — what delta should we expect for dedicated capacity?
05:49 Sara: depends on utilization but quantization often reduces GPU footprint enabling smaller instance classes or higher throughput per instance, so unit cost can drop 30-60% in many cases. We'll provide a pilot pricing estimate for dedicated/GPU pools.
06:05 Evan: any legal/security docs to share for on-prem?
06:09 Sara: yes we'll send SOC2 + architecture runbook + private deployment checklist; we'll also include a template SSO/SAML and KMS integration guide.
06:17 Alex: alright let's recap next steps.
06:20 Sara: recap: Redwood runs benchmark with INT8, GPTQ, AWQ on G5-equivalent; share AWQ tuning notes and patch; Lynx provides holdout and infra details; follow-up call week of Sept 20.
06:32 Jordan: thanks everyone, looking forward to the results.
06:35 Sara: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the shared sheet and a calendar invite. Bye.

Notes/links mentioned: benchmark sheet (redwood.co/bench/lynx-2027), AWQ tuning notes (redwood.co/awq-tuning), Private deployment guide (redwood.co/private-deploy-guide)

Transcript end.
